field_type_2026: Natural grass (hybrid) — natural turf reinforced with stitched-in synthetic fibres for FIFA consistency/durability; FIFA-spec surface installed for the 2026 World Cup (reported installed March 2026)
renovation_cost_2026: Contested / not a single agreed figure. Two distinct sourced numbers exist: (1) a $120 million package (49ers borrowed/invested via the NFL stadium fund, reported 2023) targeting premium-seating remodels and new 4K video scoreboards ahead of the 2025 season [KNBR/StadiumDB]; (2) a broader "$200 million" total renovation figure cited for the venue's 2025-2026 upgrades preparing it to host both Super Bowl LX and the World Cup [Yardbarker]. The $200M is a press characterization of overall investment, not an itemized World-Cup-specific cost. World-Cup-specific pitch-conversion cost is NOT SPECIFIED IN SOURCES.

renovations.change: FIFA-spec natural grass (hybrid, with stitched-in synthetic fibres) playing surface installed for the 2026 World Cup. Note: the prior NFL-config surface is disputed across sources (Wikipedia infobox: Bermuda grass; MartinCid: synthetic) — the 'swapped from artificial turf' framing is NOT reliably supported.

iconic_games.event: Copa América Centenario — opening match (Group A)
iconic_games.note: Tournament-opening match of the 2016 Copa América Centenario at Levi's Stadium; Cristián Zapata and James Rodríguez (pen.) scored for Colombia. Attendance 67,439. VERIFIED via Wikipedia (date, teams, score, venue, attendance all confirmed).

Historic rout at Levi's Stadium: Eduardo Vargas four, Edson Puch two, Alexis Sánchez one; ended Mexico's unbeaten run. VERIFIED via ESPN match report (date, teams, 0–7 score, venue, QF all confirmed).
Goals from Abel Hernández, an own goal, and Mathías Corujo. Attendance 40,166. VERIFIED via Wikipedia (date, teams, score, venue, attendance all confirmed).

USMNT won its sixth Gold Cup at Levi's Stadium; Altidore (FK) and Morris (88') scored, Watson equalized for Jamaica. VERIFIED via Wikipedia 2017 CONCACAF Gold Cup final (date, teams, 2–1 score, venue all confirmed).

iconic_games_note: Levi's Stadium has a genuine top-level football history, unlike most pure-NFL World Cup venues: it hosted four matches at the 2016 Copa América Centenario (including the tournament-opening USA–Colombia match and the Mexico 0–7 Chile quarter-final) and the 2017 CONCACAF Gold Cup final, plus Gold Cup group games and major international friendlies. ALL FOUR iconic games above were individually source-verified (dates, teams, scores, competitions, venue). Non-football events for context: Super Bowl 50 (Feb 7 2016), Super Bowl LX (Feb 8 2026), WrestleMania 31 (2015) — clearly labeled as non-football. In 2026 it becomes the first venue to host a Super Bowl and FIFA World Cup matches in the same calendar year.

city_history.founded: Santa Clara was founded in 1777 (Mission Santa Clara de Asís); incorporated as a city in 1852. The wider San Francisco metro dates to the 1776 Spanish presidio/mission and boomed with the 1849 Gold Rush.
city_history.significance: Levi's Stadium sits in Santa Clara, at the southern edge of Silicon Valley roughly 40 miles south of downtown San Francisco. Santa Clara is a tech-industry hub; the venue anchors the Bay Area's bid as a 2026 host region. The 'San Francisco Bay Area' host designation spans Santa Clara/San Jose and the wider Bay metropolitan area.
city_history.football_culture: Football (soccer) culture is hung on the San Francisco Bay Area metro, not the small city of Santa Clara: the region is one of the most soccer-engaged in the US, with the San Jose Earthquakes (MLS, two-time MLS Cup champions) playing nearby at PayPal Park, a large and diverse fan base (notably strong Mexican-American support for El Tri friendlies and Copa América/Gold Cup matches), and a track record of hosting major international tournaments (Copa América Centenario 2016, Gold Cup 2017). The Bay Area also has deep general sports culture across the 49ers, Giants, Warriors and A's.

stadium_history_facts: Opened July 17, 2014 as home of the San Francisco 49ers (NFL). VERIFIED (Wikipedia, HNTB).
Design architect / architect of record HNTB; built by Turner Construction. VERIFIED (HNTB, Architizer, Architect Magazine).
Construction cost approximately $1.3 billion (Wikipedia; ~$1.2 billion per some sources).
Named after Levi Strauss & Co., which acquired naming rights in 2013.
Regular seating capacity 68,500, expandable to roughly 75,000 for major events.
FIFA-confirmed 2026 World Cup configuration capacity: 68,827 (per FIFA official capacities announcement).
Hosted Super Bowl 50 (Feb 7, 2016) and Super Bowl LX (Feb 8, 2026).
Hosted four 2016 Copa América Centenario matches (incl. the opening game and Mexico 0–7 Chile QF) and the 2017 CONCACAF Gold Cup final (USA 2–1 Jamaica). All venue-verified.
Hosted WrestleMania 31 (2015) and the 2019 College Football Playoff National Championship.
Temporarily renamed 'San Francisco Bay Area Stadium' for the 2026 FIFA World Cup per FIFA's clean-venue/neutral-naming policy.
For 2026 it becomes the first venue to host a Super Bowl and FIFA World Cup matches in the same calendar year.
